newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus denies in Lockheed merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Airbus denies in Lockheed merger talks.

text.p: European airliner maker Airbus Industrie on Monday denied a British newspaper report it was in merger talks with Lockheed Martin Corp.
Bethesda, Md.-based Lockheed Martin, meanwhile, declined to comment specifically on the Airbus issue, saying only that it was pursuing a wide variety of alliances.
However, a source familiar with the company said it was not in merger talks with Airbus and did not want to team up with its European counterpart to develop a superjumbo jet.
The comments were in response to Saturday's report in The Times of London, which said the two were discussing a merger to confront a growing threat from Boeing Co. in the world market.
"We deny there are any merger talks with Lockheed," a spokeswoman for the four-nation Airbus consortium said Monday.
Airbus's four partners are negotiating changing the partnership into a single integrated company, owning its own manufacturing assets and transforming it from a marketing and sales venture.
Airbus is also looking for risk-sharing partners for its project to build a 550-seat airliner which it believes is needed to break Seattle-based Boeing's monopoly in that sector.
"We are exploring market opportunities with many aerospace companies worldwide, notably for the large airliner, the A3XX," she said.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG of Germany, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
